title: Empty 3D scene on Wayland/V3D 4.2 (RK3588) capped at ~50 fps; ~4x slower than Panda3D on identical hardware
body:
### Tested versions Godot 4.6.3-stable (official linux.arm64 build, 7d41c59c4), gl_compatibility (OpenGL ES 3.1) Tested with both Wayland (labwc) and headless display Not yet tested on earlier Godot versions ### System information CPU: Rockchip RK3588 (aarch64), 4× Cortex-A76 + 4× Cortex-A55 GPU: Broadcom V3D 4.2.14.0 (Raspberry-Pi-class, VideoCore VII) Display server: Wayland (wayland-0) at 1920×1080 @ 60 Hz, HDMI-A-1 Mesa: 25.0.7-2+rpt4 (driver: vc4) Rendering driver: opengl3_es (forced by Godot after detecting no desktop GL3) ### Issue description

The Godot main loop has a large per-frame baseline cost in gl_compatibility mode on RK3588/V3D 4.2, even with no scene objects, no scripts running, and no rendering work. On the same hardware in the same Wayland session, Panda3D 1.10.16 hits ~190 fps with an empty 1920×1080 window; Godot hits ~50 fps.

Repro measurements (1080p, vblank_mode=0):

| Setup | Engine | FPS | ms/frame | |----------------------------------------|-----------------|--------|----------| | Empty scene, Wayland, 1080p | Godot 4.6.3 | 50.0 | 20.0 | | Empty scene, headless, no display | Godot 4.6.3 | 133 | 7.5 | | Empty scene, Wayland, 1080p | Panda3D 1.10.16 | 189.84 | 5.27 | | 1 mesh (BoxMesh), Wayland, 1080p | Godot 4.6.3 | 42.5 | 16.2 | | 100 meshes (10×10 BoxMesh), Wayland | Godot 4.6.3 | 35.6 | 22.1 | | 100 meshes (10×10 BoxMesh), Wayland | Panda3D 1.10.16 | 94.12 | 10.6

Breakdown from Performance monitors in Godot:

  • Empty scene: TIME_PROCESS 9.55 ms/frame, 0 draw calls, 0 primitives
  • Adding the first mesh: +6.66 ms (16.2 − 9.5), 1 draw call, 12 primitives
  • Adding 99 more meshes: +5.91 ms total, 100 draw calls, 1200 primitives
So the cost is: ~7.5 ms baseline main-loop cost even with no scene objects (headless) +~10 ms once a Wayland display is attached +~6.7 ms the moment any mesh is in the scene (independent of mesh count) +~0.06 ms per additional mesh after the first The "first mesh costs ~6.7 ms" is the most reproducible anomaly. Per-mesh cost is essentially free, but there's a one-shot per-frame setup that fires whenever the scene has any geometry. This is reproducible both with the official Godot 4.6.3-stable download AND a self-built release template from the same source (commit 7d41c59c4), so it is not a debug-build artifact. Expected behavior An empty 3D scene on a 60 Hz display should be able to hit vsync (60 fps) on this hardware comfortably, matching what Panda3D delivers. Per-frame work with zero scene objects should be in the low single ms. ### Steps to reproduce Install Godot 4.6.3-stable for linux.arm64 from godotengine.org. Create a new project with renderer = gl_compatibility. Add a main.tscn that is completely empty (a single Node root, no children). Save. Open a terminal in the labwc Wayland session on the RK3588 hardware. Run: vblank_mode=0 ./Godot_v4.6.3-stable_linux.arm64 \ --display-driver wayland --rendering-driver opengl3 \ --max-fps 0 main.tscn Observe the wall-clock frame rate with a one-line script: extends Node var t := 0.0 var n := 0 func _process(d): t += d; n += 1 if t >= 1.0: print("fps=", n / t) t = 0; n = 0 Output will be around fps=50.0 on this hardware. For comparison, run the equivalent empty Panda3D program (see MRP) and observe ~190 fps. To also see the "any mesh = +6.7 ms" effect: drop a single MeshInstance3D with a BoxMesh into the empty scene. Wall-clock fps drops from ~50 to ~42; Performance.RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME reports 1, RENDER_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES_IN_FRAME reports 12. Minimal reproduction project (MRP) See attached mrp_empty_scene.zip — contains: project.godot — gl_compatibility, window 1920×1080, autoload = fps_reporter.gd main.tscn — empty scene (just a Node root) fps_reporter.gd — prints fps=… to stdout every second compare_panda.py — same empty scene in Panda3D for head-to-head timing To reproduce: unzip mrp_empty_scene.zip cd mrp_empty_scene vblank_mode=0 /path/to/Godot_v4.6.3-stable_linux.arm64 \ --display-driver wayland --rendering-driver opengl3 --max-fps 0 Expected: fps=50 (or whatever half of the display refresh is — labwc appears to be throttling to ~50 Hz on this hardware). Same scene in Panda3D: ~190 fps. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp_empty_scene.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28624067/mrp_empty_scene.zip)
